documents.title: Confidential Information Memorandum — Helix Specialty Chemicals ("Project Aurora")
documents.summary: Lazard Middle Market CIM for Helix Specialty Chemicals ("Project Aurora"), a 39-year-old independent specialty chemicals distributor headquartered in Cleveland, OH. Helix is the #3 independent distributor by revenue in North America and #1 in its core Midwest/Southeast geography, with $725M LTM revenue and $95M LTM Adj. EBITDA (13.1% margin). The business is 100% family-owned (3rd generation Beckwith family) and is being brought to market as a full sale, with CEO Tom Beckwith open to rollover equity. Key investment highlights include strong customer diversification (top 10 = 14% of revenue), 94% customer retention, a 14.8% revenue CAGR (FY22–FY25 LTM), expanding EBITDA margins (10.9% → 13.1%), a differentiated technical sales force, and a robust M&A pipeline of 10+ proprietary targets. The transaction process targets IOIs in January 2026 and closing in Q2 2026.

Organic expansion into Pacific Northwest, Florida, and Mountain West ($200M+ revenue capture identified)
Active M&A pipeline of 10+ proprietary targets in specialty chemicals and adjacent lines
Onshoring tailwind and manufacturing capex recovery boosting industrial end-market demand
Regulatory tightening and infrastructure investment driving water treatment segment growth
Technical sales force (52 chemical engineers) generating 280bps gross margin premium vs. commodity distribution
risks: Oil & gas end market (18% of revenue) exposes company to commodity price cyclicality

Family-controlled business transitioning to institutional ownership; management continuity dependent on CEO rollover

documents.title: Project Aurora — Historical Financials (FY20-FY25 LTM)

Stockholders' equity is attributed to the Beckwith family, indicating a founder/family-owned business. Several addback items (family expenses, legal one-time, pre-opening costs) are consistent with a founder-transition scenario.

documents.title: Project Aurora — LBO Model (Base Case)
documents.summary: LBO financial model for Project Aurora prepared by Atlas Crossing Partners Fund IV in January 2026, with an anticipated entry date of April 14, 2026. The model reflects a $1.1B enterprise value acquisition of a company (founder Tom Beckwith / Beckwith family) at an implied 11.6x LTM EBITDA multiple ($95M LTM Adj. EBITDA). Debt financing is led by a $580M senior unitranche (Antares + Twin Brook), with $145M Atlas Crossing equity and $123M Beckwith rollover equity. The base case projects revenue growing from $725M LTM to ~$1.19B by FY30, with EBITDA margins expanding from ~13.1% to ~16.3%. The model includes bolt-on M&A assumptions ($25M–$135M annual bolt-on revenue), organic growth decelerating from 8% to 5.5%, and $405M in total debt paydown over the 5-year hold. Returns sensitivity spans a downside exit at $110M EBITDA / 9.5x to an upside of $180M EBITDA / 12.5x.

growth_drivers: Organic revenue growth (~8% in FY26, decelerating to ~5.5% by FY30)
Bolt-on M&A contributing $25M–$135M in incremental annual revenue
Gross margin expansion from 31.6% to 33.4% over hold period
EBITDA margin expansion from ~13.7% (FY26B) to ~16.3% (FY30B)
Significant debt paydown ($55M–$110M per year) to reduce leverage and enhance equity returns
risks: High entry leverage (~6.1x EV/EBITDA funded by $580M unitranche)
Execution risk on bolt-on acquisition program ($390M cumulative bolt-on revenue assumed)
Organic growth deceleration assumed; underperformance would compress returns
Floating rate debt (SOFR + 525 bps) exposes model to interest rate sensitivity
Founder rollover (Tom Beckwith) suggests founder-transition dynamic with potential key-man risk

documents.title: Exit Recommendation — Halcyon Pet Foods, Inc. | Atlas Crossing Partners Fund II IC Memorandum
documents.summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund II exit IC memo recommending sale of Halcyon Pet Foods, Inc. to Cabrillo Holdings (Mars-affiliated) for $890M enterprise value (14.5x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $61.4M). The all-cash stock purchase transaction is targeting an April 14, 2023 close. Fund II invested $104M in equity (initial $95M in Sep 2017 + $9M bolt-on for Vesta Treats in Jun 2020) and expects cumulative proceeds of $355M (including $21M Q3 2021 dividend recap), yielding 3.5x gross MOIC and 28.4% gross IRR on a ~5.5-year hold. Net MOIC is 2.8x and net IRR is 23.1%. Key value creation drivers include DTC channel build (subscriber count grew 6.5x), organic revenue growth (51% of equity value creation), multiple expansion from 11.0x to 14.5x (29%), and the Vesta Treats bolt-on (8%). Revenue grew from $132M to $328M and EBITDA from $25.9M to $61.4M over the hold period. The memo notes three competing final bids and recommends Cabrillo for highest bid, all-cash structure, and strategic synergies with Mars global distribution.

key_quotes.quote: Returns: 3.5x gross MOIC and ~28% gross IRR to Atlas Crossing Fund II — a top-quartile outcome and the highest MOIC delivered by the fund to date.

DTC build was the single largest value driver. Hired Head of DTC in Q1 2018; rebuilt tech stack 2018–2019 (CDP, marketing automation, owned subscription engine). Subscriber count grew 6.5× over the hold period.

Premium-pet category multiples are currently elevated (clean assets pricing 14–17x) but show early signs of moderation as inflation persists and discretionary consumer spend faces pressure... Further hold increases the risk of negative multiple drift outweighing incremental EBITDA growth.

Plan was $4–6M over 18 months; actual investment was $11M over 24 months. Should have approved the larger envelope at close. Lesson: for DTC-heavy plans, double the IT-investment budget at underwriting and treat ahead-of-curve infra as defensive.

Held to a single co-packer for wet food until Q4 2021; freight pressure 2021–2022 caused service-level dips. Should have moved to dual-source wet by mid-2020. Cost in lost revenue (quantified internally at ~$8M).

documents.title: Investment Committee Memorandum — Initial Investment Recommendation: Cardinal Filtration Co.
documents.summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund I entry IC memo recommending the acquisition of Cardinal Filtration Co., a regional industrial filtration distributor headquartered in Akron, OH, at an enterprise value of $175M (7.5x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $23.3M). The investment thesis centers on a disciplined roll-up strategy in the highly fragmented ~$8B US industrial filtration distribution market, private-label penetration expansion (9% → 25%), supplier consolidation, and organic revenue growth in defensive end markets. The base case underwrites 4 bolt-on acquisitions over a 5-year hold, targeting exit EBITDA of $52M at an 8.5x multiple ($442M EV), implying a 4.0x MOIC and 32% gross IRR. Deal team: S. Kowalski (MD), R. Patel (Principal), L. Chen (VP).

key_quotes.quote: We see a clear path to 2.5–3.5x MOIC over a 5-year hold through a disciplined roll-up strategy in a highly fragmented category, alongside operational improvements in private-label penetration and supplier consolidation.

The $8B US industrial filtration distribution market is served by ~600 sub-$50M-revenue regional distributors. Top 10 hold less than 20% share. We have line-of-sight on 12–15 attractive bolt-on targets within Cardinal's strike zone.

Cardinal currently sells 91% branded product (Donaldson, Parker, 3M, etc.). Top-quartile peers operate at 25–35% private label. Migration over 3 years to 25% PL implies +280bps gross margin expansion (vs. 31.5% LTM).

70% of revenue serves regulated or essential industries (water treatment, power gen, F&B manufacturing). Filtration is a consumable that gets replaced regardless of macro cycles. Stress-tested through 2008–09 downturn: revenue declined just 6% peak-to-trough.

Outreach to 14 prioritized targets; 9 returned signed NDAs and provided initial financials. 5 Tier 1 targets have indicated openness to a transaction at 5.0–5.5x EBITDA on combined revenue of $95M. Three of the five owners are >65 years old with no clear succession plan.

growth_drivers: Roll-up of 12–15 fragmented regional bolt-on targets
Private-label penetration expansion from 9% to 25% (200–400bps GM uplift)
Supplier consolidation from 47 to top-10 suppliers (80–120bps GM savings)
Organic revenue growth in water treatment and F&B end markets
Recurring/contracted revenue model with 87% repeat-revenue share
SG&A leverage via centralized purchasing, IT modernization, DC network optimization
risks: Roll-up integration execution risk
Supplier concentration (top 5 = 38% of spend)
Asian import competition in commodity filtration SKUs
Donaldson/Parker direct-to-customer pressure on large accounts
Industrial cycle exposure (mitigated by 70% defensive end-market mix)
Working capital intensity (71-day cycle)

documents.title: Exit Recommendation — Cardinal Filtration Co.
documents.summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund I IC exit memo recommending the sale of Cardinal Filtration Co. to Donaldson Company, Inc. (NYSE: DCI) for $560M enterprise value (9.5x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $58.9M). The deal represents a 5.3-year hold from September 2014, delivering 3.2x gross MOIC and ~26.1% gross IRR (2.6x / 21.2% net). Entry thesis centered on industrial filtration roll-up was largely delivered: 4 bolt-ons completed, gross margin expanded 320bps, private-label penetration grew from 9% to 28%, and revenue scaled from $186M to $472M. Operating margin was flat (thesis miss due to bolt-on mix shift). Sale process run by Baird yielded three final bids; Donaldson selected at $560M all-cash, no financing condition.

key_quotes.quote: Returns: 3.2x gross MOIC and ~26% gross IRR — top-quartile outcome and the highest absolute proceeds in Fund I.

Cardinal is at peak scale relative to standalone optionality. Further organic growth requires geographic expansion into the West and Southeast, where additional capital deployment ($60M+) and integration complexity would extend the hold by 2–3 years.
key_quotes.topic: Why now — strategic rationale for timing

key_quotes.quote: Marketing was structured around Cardinal's scarcity value as a $470M-revenue industrial filtration platform with 12 distribution centers and a successful 5-acquisition rollup track record.
Operating margin: +200bps over hold [plan] — Flat (Y/Y; mix shift from bolt-ons) — Miss — mix effect.
Selected Donaldson — strategic, all-cash, willing to drop financing condition, and providing material premium for product-line complementarity and manufacturing synergies.

growth_drivers: Roll-up M&A strategy (4 bolt-on acquisitions over hold)
Private-label penetration growth from 9% to 28%
Geographic expansion: 4 to 12 distribution centers
Customer base growth from 3,400 to 11,200
Multiple expansion from 7.5x to 9.5x
Strategic buyer premium from Donaldson for product-line complementarity
risks: Operating margin flat vs. +200bps thesis (mix shift from bolt-ons)
EnvioGuard synergies still in progress at exit
Further organic growth would require $60M+ additional capital and 2-3 year hold extension

documents.title: Cardinal Filtration Co. — Management Presentation
documents.summary: Management presentation prepared for final-round buyer meetings in June–July 2019 as part of Cardinal Filtration Co.'s exit process. Cardinal is a national industrial filtration products distributor headquartered in Akron, OH, founded in 1987 and acquired by Atlas Crossing Partners in September 2014. Over the ~5-year hold, the company grew revenue from $186M to $472M LTM through organic growth and four bolt-on acquisitions, with EBITDA expanding from $23.3M to $58.9M. Key value creation levers include a disciplined roll-up M&A playbook, private-label (CardinalGuard) expansion from 9% to 28% of revenue with a 600bps GM premium, and geographic DC footprint growth from 4 to 12 locations. Future opportunities highlighted include further geographic expansion, private-label penetration to 35–40%, engineered solutions/service revenue growth, and a potential Canadian distribution hub.

growth_drivers: Roll-up M&A of regional distributors at 5–6x pre-synergy EBITDA with rapid purchasing integration
CardinalGuard private-label expansion: 9% → 28% of revenue, targeting 35–40% penetration
Geographic expansion into Pacific Northwest, Mountain West, and Mid-Atlantic via new DCs
Engineered solutions / service revenue growth from 9% toward 15–18% of revenue mix
International distribution opportunity via Toronto DC serving Canadian customers
risks: Integration risk from four bolt-on acquisitions and ongoing M&A playbook
Private-label concentration risk and dependency on CardinalGuard margin premium
Founder/family dynamic with CEO Steve Brandt (founder's son, 32-year tenure)

documents.title: Cardinal Filtration Co. — Sell-Side Quality of Earnings Summary
documents.summary: Grant Thornton Transaction Advisory Services prepared this sell-side Quality of Earnings (VDD QofE) for Cardinal Filtration Co. on behalf of Atlas Crossing Partners (ACP) in support of the May 2019 exit/sale process. The report bridges LTM March 2019 reported EBITDA of $52.4M to a preliminary adjusted EBITDA of $58.9M through $6.5M in addbacks (CEO comp normalization, EnvioGuard integration costs, non-recurring legal/advisory, phantom equity amortization, D&A reclassification) offset by a $0.6M revenue timing haircut. Key findings confirm high revenue quality (87% recurring, no customer >6% of revenue), supportable and well-documented adjustments, normalized working capital (NWC peg of $66M), and a structural private-label margin premium for the CardinalGuard product line (40.8% GM vs. 34.3% branded).

key_quotes.quote: 87% of LTM revenue is from accounts with >2-year tenure. Top 50 customers represent 47% of revenue; all 50 have been customers for >5 years. No single customer exceeds 6% of revenue.
Total addbacks of $6.5M against reported EBITDA of $52.4M are well-documented. The EnvioGuard integration costs ($2.8M) are evidenced by third-party invoices and internal project tracking.

CardinalGuard gross margin of 40.8% vs. 34.3% for branded — a 650bps premium. Margin advantage is structural: proprietary specifications, single-source manufacturing agreements, and customer-spec lock-in.
NWC as % of revenue has been stable at 14.2–14.8% over FY17–LTM. Proposed NWC peg of $66M reflects trailing-12-month average.

growth_drivers: High recurring revenue base (87% of LTM revenue from accounts with >2-year tenure)
No single customer exceeds 6% of revenue — diversified customer base
CardinalGuard private-label gross margin premium of 650bps vs. branded (40.8% vs. 34.3%)
Structural private-label advantage via proprietary specs, single-source manufacturing, and customer-spec lock-in
risks: Q1 2019 customer prepayment (pull-forward revenue) — $0.6M non-recurring benefit reversed
EnvioGuard acquisition caused temporary NWC spike of ~$3M (now normalized)
Phantom equity settled at exit — one-time cash outflow

documents.title: Project Titan — Confidential Information Memorandum
documents.summary: CIM prepared by Robert W. Baird & Co. on behalf of Atlas Crossing Partners Fund I for the sale of Cardinal Filtration Co. ("Project Titan"). Cardinal is a national industrial filtration products distributor headquartered in Akron, OH, serving 11,200 customers across manufacturing, power generation, water treatment, F&B, and HVAC. key_quotes.quote: Cardinal has grown from a single-location, $186M-revenue business at ACP's entry in 2014 to a 12-distribution-center national platform generating $472M in LTM revenue and $58.9M in Adj. EBITDA through disciplined roll-up M&A, private-label expansion, and supplier consolidation.
Cardinal's proprietary product line (CardinalGuard) grew from 9% of revenue in 2014 to 28% in LTM 2019, carrying a 600bps gross margin premium vs. branded products.
4 bolt-ons acquired at average 5.5x pre-synergy / 3.9x post-synergy EBITDA multiple. Each acquisition was fully integrated within 18 months.
Industrial filtration is a consumable — maintenance schedules are driven by regulatory compliance and equipment warranty requirements, not capex cycles.
Average customer tenure of 11.4 years reflects structural lock-in from technical service and engineered-solutions relationships.

growth_drivers: Roll-up M&A playbook — 4 bolt-ons acquired at avg. 5.5x pre-synergy / 3.9x post-synergy EBITDA
Private-label expansion: CardinalGuard grew from 9% to 28% of revenue, carrying 600bps GM premium

Defensive, essential end-market exposure (70% regulated/essential industries)
Supplier consolidation driving 80–120bps gross margin uplift on acquired businesses

documents.title: Investment Committee Memorandum — Initial Investment Recommendation: Precision Asset Inspections, Inc.
documents.summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund II entry IC memo recommending acquisition of Precision Asset Inspections, Inc., a Houston-based non-destructive testing (NDT) and asset integrity management services provider, at an $82M enterprise value (8.7x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $9.4M). The investment thesis centers on a geographic roll-up of regional NDT firms, commercialization of the proprietary Vantage IQ SaaS-like inspection platform, and EBITDA margin expansion from ~18% toward peer levels of 22–25%. The base case underwrites a 3.0x MOIC / 23% IRR at a $310M exit EV over a ~5-year hold, with identified bolt-on pipeline of 12 targets across Permian Basin, Gulf Coast, and Appalachian corridors.

key_quotes.quote: We underwrite a 3.0–4.0x MOIC over a 5–6 year hold through geographic roll-up of regional NDT firms, completion and commercialization of the Vantage IQ technology platform, and expansion into the adjacent offshore and utility inspection markets.

Precision's inspection revenue is therefore driven by regulatory calendars, not operator capex budgets. Revenue declined only 8% during the 2020 COVID shutdown — inspections were deferred, not cancelled, and catch-up drove a strong 2021 rebound.

We see a clear path to $5M+ annual SaaS subscription revenue by Year 4 as we migrate existing MSA clients onto the platform. Data switching costs and inspection history depth create durable retention.

The US energy infrastructure NDT market is served by ~400 regional firms with <$20M revenue each. We have identified 12 target acquisitions in the Permian Basin, Gulf Coast, and Appalachian pipeline corridors — the three highest-density NDT demand markets.

Precision's 18.1% EBITDA margin at entry is below the 22–25% margins of comparably scaled TIC peers (Bureau Veritas, Intertek). Margin expansion levers: (a) Vantage IQ reduces per-inspection labor cost by 20%+; (b) technician utilization improvement from 62% to 75–78%; (c) fixed-overhead absorption as revenue scales.

growth_drivers: Regulatory-mandated inspection demand (PHMSA, API standards) providing non-discretionary revenue base
Vantage IQ proprietary SaaS-like platform targeting $5M+ annual subscription revenue by Year 4
Geographic roll-up of 12 identified regional NDT targets in Permian Basin, Gulf Coast, and Appalachian corridor
Technician utilization improvement from 62% toward peer best-in-class 75–78%
In-house ASNT-accredited training center to scale certified technician pipeline
Expansion into adjacent offshore and utility inspection markets
risks: Vantage IQ platform delivery risk — 70% complete, requires $6–8M additional investment over 18 months
Energy sector cyclicality — 44% of revenue tied to oil & gas E&P and midstream operators
Technician labor scarcity — tight ASNT certification pipeline vulnerable to competitor poaching
Integration complexity across geographically dispersed bolt-on service centers

documents.title: Investment Committee Memorandum — Initial Investment Recommendation — Wholesum Foods Distribution, Inc.
documents.summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III IC entry memo recommending acquisition of a majority controlling interest in Wholesum Foods Distribution, Inc. at $710M enterprise value (9.8x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $72.4M). Wholesum is the largest US specialty foodservice distributor focused on Hispanic, Asian, and Mediterranean/Italian product lines, serving ~3,500 restaurant and retail customers from 12 DCs. Atlas Crossing is contributing $155M equity; the Gonzales family is rolling $125M (22%). Key thesis themes include market consolidation via bolt-on M&A, private-label margin expansion, tech modernization (NetSuite/WMS), and organic growth in high-growth ethnic food segments. Target 4-year hold with base case 3.4x MOIC / 35.8% gross IRR at a $1.22B exit EV.

key_quotes.quote: The Investment Team recommends the Investment Committee approve the acquisition of a majority controlling interest in Wholesum Foods Distribution, Inc. ("Wholesum") by Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III, L.P. at an enterprise value of $710 million, representing 9.8x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of $72.4M.

US specialty / ethnic foodservice distribution is growing at 8–10% CAGR vs. mainstream foodservice distribution at 3–4%. Drivers: shifting US demographics (Hispanic/Latino market is now 19% of US population, projected 28% by 2050).

Wholesum is only 8% private label today vs. 18–25% at scaled mainstream foodservice distributors and 15-20% at specialty grocery distributors. Migration to 18% PL over 4–5 years implies +220bps GM expansion.
Wholesum demonstrated resilience through COVID: revenue declined 11% in 2020 (vs. 25%+ for mainstream foodservice distributors) and fully recovered by Q3 2021.

FTI's IT assessment confirms the urgency of ERP modernization. Current system (custom Visual Basic, last major upgrade 2007) cannot support: (a) advanced demand forecasting / inventory optimization; (b) integrated digital ordering; (c) multi-DC SKU rationalization.

growth_drivers: Outsized growth in specialty/ethnic foodservice distribution (8–10% CAGR vs. 3–4% mainstream)
Fragmented market with 8+ identified bolt-on targets in adjacent ethnic categories and underserved geographies
Private-label expansion from 8% to 18% implying +220bps GM expansion
Tech modernization (NetSuite ERP + Manhattan WMS) expected to unlock $9–11M incremental EBITDA
Demographic tailwinds: Hispanic/Latino population projected at 28% of US by 2050; Asian-American population growing rapidly
risks: Family/founder transition risk (Roberto → Carmen Gonzales Diaz as CEO)
ERP modernization execution risk (legacy custom Visual Basic system)
Potential consolidation by Sysco/US Foods specialty arms
Labor cost inflation and fulfillment labor availability

documents.title: Project Ember – Cascade Outdoor Brands Confidential Information Memorandum
documents.summary: Harris Williams sell-side CIM for Cascade Outdoor Brands ("Project Ember"), a Denver, CO-based premium designer and manufacturer of technical outdoor hardgoods (tents, shelters, ultralight cookware) sold under two owned brands — Ridgeline (mid-market, $95 ASP) and Summit Series (premium, $285 ASP). LTM Apr 2024 revenue of $112M and Adj. EBITDA of $14.0M (12.5% margin). DTC e-commerce represents 44% of revenue, up from 29% three years ago. The Company has 58K paid loyalty members, 3 issued patents, international revenue in 22 countries, and an OEM/licensing royalty stream ($3.2M ARR). Indicative EV implied at ~$175M (12.5x LTM EBITDA). Sale process initiated April 2024; closing targeted Q3 2024.

key_quotes.quote: Ridgeline targets weekend campers and trail runners (ASP $95); Summit Series serves thru-hikers and mountaineers (ASP $285) — Brand separation prevents channel conflict; Ridgeline sold at REI and Target; Summit Series exclusively at specialty and DTC.
DTC e-commerce grew from 29% to 44% of revenue over 3 years; gross margin 15pp higher than wholesale channel.
Subscription loyalty program ('Summit Club') with 58K paying members at $49/yr; 91% year-1 retention.

AeroShield™ fabric technology (2 patents): 22% lighter than competitive Dyneema composites at comparable strength... HexLite™ cookware alloy (1 patent): 18% lighter than titanium with equivalent heat distribution; $3.2M in royalty-bearing licenses to 2 OEM brands.
International revenue +34% YoY, led by Germany, Japan, and Australia; 22 distributor relationships in place.
